newsitem.title: INDIA: India ICICI to raise $500 million loan.
newsitem.headline: India ICICI to raise $500 million loan.

text.p: The Industrial Credit and Investment Corp of India Ltd (ICICI) said on Tuesday it received government approval to initiate a global medium term note (GMTN) programme to raise upto $500 million.
ICICI is the first Indian financial institution to receive such an approval, it said in a statement.
ICICI is one of India's leading term lending banks.

"The GMTN programme is an umbrella borrowing programme allowing ICICI to access Asian, European and U.S. markets on an ongoing basis with a variety of instruments of varying maturities in multiple currencies under a single comprehensive set of documentation," ICICI said.
It would help enhance ICICI's profile as a frequent borrower by ensuring a continuous presence in the international market and also broaden its base of international investors.
It will offer flexibility in borrowings by allowing quick access brief windows, ICICI said.
ICICI proposes to launch the programme with an inaugural issue of subordinated floating rate notes (FRN) for $100 million soon, the bank said.
The instrument is proposed to be structured as a floating rate note linked to the LIBOR with a final maturity of 10 years.

The FRN issue would enhance ICICI's capital adequacy ratio without any equity dilution. The FRN issue has been rated at the same level as ICICI's senior debt at Baa3 by Moody's Investor Services, ICICI said.

ICICI has appointed SBC Warburg and Citibank as joint arrangers of the GMTN programme and as joint lead managers for the FRN issue. The FRN issue is scheduled for launch in the first week of March 1997.
